description: parse scans entries and normalizes values; manifest_for_ids maps IDs to last bibliography entries, walks wanted order, returns JSONL and missing IDs. run_ids writes only when no IDs missing. run groups title/proceedings/abstract matches by topic and minimum priority, sharing first matching prefix and per-entry slug. inverse: Missing IDs exclude destination write in run_ids; foreign authority excludes nonempty anthology_id. No URLs are fetched. Inner exclusions derived from source, not universal malformed-input safety.
Rows admit all BibTeX and requested lists yielding same last-ID map and projection. Braces, whitespace, shadowed entries and duplicate requests are unrecoverable; output is many-to-one.
limitations: Partial syntax and finite fixtures, not universal semantic proof.
Value full workflow, arbitrary manifests and external IO failures are not exercised.
state: Bounded UTF-8, representable depth/indices, available allocation. Missing fields read empty. read_ids limits priority to 1..3; row accepts any u8. Host identity requires HTTP(S) and exact case-insensitive aclanthology.org authority, then last query/fragment-free path segment; no port/userinfo support. Topic run requires nonempty anthology_id for JSONL admission, preserving all matched abstract listings. Writes are not transactional. Exact-host admission and id extraction do not normalize row URLs: row appends '.pdf' to the original URL text, so query/fragment-bearing official URLs need not produce usable canonical PDF paths. The actual plan/check join fixture uses a query-free canonical path.
